title: Who really owns Tung Tung Tung Sahur?
key_facts: Innovatex Labs LLC filed a US application for the name TUNG TUNG TUNG SAHUR in May 2025, for toys including plush dolls and figurines; it filed separate applications for other "brainrot" names such as Tralalero Tralala.
The US Patent and Trademark Office published the application for opposition on 15 Sep; Mementum Lab, the agency representing the character's creator, asked for more time to oppose.
The office granted the extension through 13 Jan 2027, per its docket; no trademark is registered yet and no formal opposition has been filed.
Mementum has its own pending US trademark application for TUNG TUNG SAHUR, including a stylised bat-holding version.

Mementum is also in a lawsuit with the companies behind the Roblox game Steal a Brainrot, who argue AI-generated works may not get copyright without enough human authorship; unresolved, per The Guardian.
The character was created in 2025 by an Indonesian teenager known as Noxa using OpenAI's image tool.
quote_evidence: Another company is seeking to trademark its name in the United States, adding a fresh complication to an ongoing dispute over the character's rights.
The USPTO granted the extension through January 13, 2027, according to the agency's official docket.

Copyright and trademark law address different things, and a trademark application for a name does not automatically establish ownership of every image, video, or other creative work associated with that character.
why_it_matters_hint: A second party now seeks rights to the character's name for toys, while the copyright question over AI-made characters is still unsettled.
event_date: Application filed May 2025; published for opposition 15 Sep 2026; extension to 13 Jan 2027
notes: Older filings reported late: the 15 Sep 2026 publication and the extension granted about a week later predate the window. Our 7 Oct 2026 edition carried The Guardian report on the related lawsuit (item 107).
